definitions.explanation: Literally the cord that closed an old-style money pouch; figuratively, control over spending. Used in set phrases about being tight with money or about who manages a household's money.

examples.japanese: {財布|さいふ}の{紐|ひも}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{固|かた}い→固い：12090_katai⟧。
examples.english: He keeps a tight hold on the purse strings.

examples.japanese: ⟦{我|わ}が{家|や}→我が家：03038_wagaya⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{妻|つま}→妻：01005_tsuma⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{財布|さいふ}の{紐|ひも}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{握|にぎ}っている→握る：02383_nigiru⟧。
examples.english: In our house my wife holds the purse strings.

examples.japanese: ⟦{景気|けいき}→景気：02694_keiki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{悪|わる}く→悪い：00908_warui⟧⟦なり→なる：01970_naru⟧、⟦{消費者|しょうひしゃ}→消費者：09866_shouhisha⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{財布|さいふ}の{紐|ひも}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{締|し}め→締める：10057_shimeru⟧{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: As the economy worsened, consumers began tightening their purse strings.

notes:
Almost always appears with a verb or adjective in one of a handful of fixed phrases.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {財布|さいふ}の{紐|ひも}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{固|かた}い→固い：12090_katai⟧: careful with money, tight-fisted
- {財布|さいふ}の{紐|ひも}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{緩|ゆる}む→緩む：10056_yurumu⟧: to loosen up and spend freely
- {財布|さいふ}の{紐|ひも}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{締|し}める→締める：10057_shimeru⟧: to tighten one's belt
- {財布|さいふ}の{紐|ひも}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{握|にぎ}る→握る：02383_nigiru⟧: to control the household money

News writing uses these of consumers in general: ⟦{消費者|しょうひしゃ}→消費者：09866_shouhisha⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{財布|さいふ}の{紐|ひも}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{固|かた}い→固い：12090_katai⟧ (consumers are holding back on spending).
